translations.text: King Astyages was gathered to his ancestors, and Cyrus the Persian took over his kingdom.
Daniel held a position of honor with the king and lived with the king, and all the king’s friends praised him.
The Babylonians had an idol named Bel. Every day they provided him with twelve ardabs of fine flour, forty rams, and six metretes of wine.
The king himself revered him and went every day to bow down before him. But Daniel worshiped God. The king said to Daniel, “Why do you not worship Bel, my god?”

Daniel said to him, “I do not worship an image, an idol, or a carved figure, because it is the work of human hands. Instead, I revere the living God, who made heaven and earth and is Lord over all flesh. He is the one I worship.”
The king said to Daniel, “Does it not seem to you that Bel is alive? Do you not see that he eats and drinks every day?”
Then Daniel laughed and said to the king, “Do not be mistaken, O king. This thing is clay on the inside and bronze on the outside. It has never eaten or drunk anything in its life.”
Then the king became angry, called Bel’s priests, and said to them, “Unless you tell me who eats all these provisions, you will die.
But if you show me that Bel is the one who eats them, Daniel will die, because he has blasphemed against Bel.” Daniel said to the king, “Let it be as you say, O king.”
There were seventy priests of Bel, not counting their wives and children. The king and Daniel went to Bel’s temple.
The priests said to the king, “Look, we are going outside. But you, O king, set out the food for Bel, mix the wine and set it out, then shut the door and seal it with your signet ring.
Come early in the morning. If you do not find that Bel has eaten all the food, let us die. But if Bel has eaten it, let Daniel die, since he has blasphemed against us.”
They were confident because they had made a secret entrance beneath the table. Through it they would go in and out, eat everything set out for Bel, and take away whatever was left over.

After Bel’s priests went out, the king brought food, filled the table, and set it before Bel. He filled the vessels with wine according to their custom and went out. Daniel said to his servants, “Bring me ashes.” They brought him ashes, and he sifted them through a sieve throughout Bel’s temple in the king’s presence. The king watched and went out. He shut the door, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and Daniel’s signet ring.
During the night the priests came as usual, with their wives and children. They ate everything that had been set out for Bel and drank the wine.
The king rose early in the morning, with Daniel beside him, and they went there.
The king said to Daniel, “Are the seals intact, Daniel?” Daniel said, “They are intact, my lord the king.”

When he opened the door, the king looked intently at the table and saw that everything set out for Bel had been eaten. From outside the doorway he cried out loudly, “You are great, Bel! There is not the slightest deceit in you!”
Then Daniel laughed and held the king back from going inside for a moment. Daniel said to the king, “Look, my lord the king, and examine the ground. Whose footprints are these?”
The king said, “I see footprints of men, women, and children on the floor.”

Then the king became angry and seized the priests, their wives, and their children. They showed the king the secret entrance they had, through which they would go in and out and eat everything set out on the table for Bel.
The king killed them all and gave Bel to Daniel as a gift. Daniel smashed him and demolished his temple.
There was also a great dragon there, which the Babylonians worshiped.
The king said to Daniel, “Now, about this one, you cannot say that he is not a god. Worship him, because he is a living god.”
Daniel said to the king, “I worship the Lord God, because he is the living God.”
“But you, O king, give me authority over him, and I will kill this dragon without a sword or a club.” The king said to him, “He is given over to you.”

Daniel took pitch, hair, and fat, boiled them together, made balls from them, and threw them into the dragon’s mouth. The dragon swallowed them, burst open, and died. Daniel said, “Look at what you worship, Babylonians!”

When the Babylonians heard this, they were deeply upset. They gathered against the king and turned on him, saying to one another, “The king has become a Jew! He has smashed Bel, killed the dragon, and killed the priests.”
They came to the king and said to him, “Either hand Daniel over to us, or we will kill you and your household.”
The king saw that they had all risen against him together. He was put under pressure and was forced to hand Daniel over to them.
They took Daniel away and threw him into the lions’ den. He remained there for six days, so that the lions would become hungry and eat him.
There were seven lions in that pit, and they were given two bodies and two rams a day. But during those days they were given nothing to eat, so that they would become hungry and eat Daniel.
Now the prophet Habakkuk was in Judea. He had cooked a stew, broken bread into a bowl, and put the stew in it. He set out to take it to the reapers in the field.
The angel of the Lord said to him, “Go, take this food you are carrying to Daniel, who has been thrown into the lions’ pit in Babylon.”
Habakkuk said, “My lord, I have never seen Babylon, and I do not know the den.”
The angel placed his hand on Habakkuk’s head, lifted him by the hair of his head, and set him in Babylon above the pit, by the power of the Holy Spirit.
Habakkuk called out and said, “Daniel, Daniel, get up and take this meal that God has sent you.”
Daniel said, “God has remembered me and has not withdrawn his mercy from me, for I know that you do not abandon those who love you.”
Daniel got up and ate. At that very moment the angel took Habakkuk and set him down in the place from which he had taken him before.
On the seventh day the king came to mourn for Daniel, because he was grieving over him. He came to the pit, looked into it, and saw Daniel sitting there.
He cried out loudly and said, “Great is the God of Daniel!”

He brought him up out of the pit. Then he threw Daniel’s enemies, those who had slandered him and wanted to kill him, into the pit. At that very moment the lions devoured them in front of the king and Daniel.
